title: Lothal: Harappan Port Town and Visiting Guide
seoTitle: Lothal: Harappan Port Town & Visiting Guide | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Visit Lothal, the Harappan site near Ahmedabad: the basin often called a dockyard, the acropolis and bead workshops, the ASI museum, how to reach and what to know.
description: A visitor's guide to Lothal in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat: a Harappan town excavated from 1955, its large basin interpreted by most archaeologists as a dockyard (and by some as a reservoir), the acropolis, lower town and bead-making workshops, the ASI site museum, the National Maritime Heritage Complex under development nearby, how to reach and tips.
dek: Lothal is one of the most important Harappan sites in India, a trading town with what many archaeologists see as the world's earliest known dockyard.

hero.alt: Excavated brick foundations at the Harappan site of Lothal, Gujarat

intro: Lothal lies in the plains of Ahmedabad district, about 80 km south-west of Ahmedabad, near the Gulf of Khambhat. It was excavated by the ASI under S. R. Rao between 1955 and 1962, revealing a planned Harappan town occupied in the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE.

Its best-known feature is a large brick-lined basin connected to an old river channel. Most archaeologists interpret it as a dockyard, and recent studies of sediments and microfossils have supported that view, though some scholars have argued it was a water reservoir. Lothal is on India's Tentative List for UNESCO nomination.
quickAnswer: Lothal, about 80 km from Ahmedabad, is a Harappan town excavated between 1955 and 1962. Its large brick basin is interpreted by most archaeologists as a dockyard, the earliest known, though a minority see it as a reservoir. Visitors can see the basin, the acropolis, the lower town and bead workshops, and the ASI museum, which is closed on Fridays. Visit from November to February.
takeaways: About 80 km from Ahmedabad; allow half a day.
The brick basin is widely interpreted as a dockyard; some scholars have proposed a reservoir.
The ASI site museum is closed on Fridays.
The site is exposed; visit in the cool winter months and early in the day.
A National Maritime Heritage Complex is being developed nearby.

items.name: The basin
body: A large rectangular brick-lined basin on the east side of the town, with an inlet and a spillway.

items.name: The acropolis and lower town
body: A raised area with drains, baths and a warehouse, and the residential lower town laid out in blocks.

items.name: Bead-making workshops
body: Evidence of a bead industry using carnelian and other stones, traded widely.

items.name: The site museum
body: Seals, beads, pottery, tools and ornaments found at Lothal, with models of the town.

sections.heading: Evidence and interpretation
paras: What is established: Lothal was a planned Harappan settlement with a drainage system, a warehouse, craft workshops and a large basin connected to a water channel, and objects found here show links with other Harappan sites and wider trade.

What is interpreted: whether the basin served ships (a dockyard) or stored fresh water. The dockyard reading is the more widely accepted, and has been strengthened by recent scientific studies; we present it as the leading interpretation rather than settled fact.

sections.heading: How to reach
list: From Ahmedabad: about 80 km by road, around two hours.
The nearest railway stations are Lothal-Bhurkhi and Dholka; road travel is more practical.
Combine it with Nal Sarovar bird sanctuary on a winter day trip.

sections.heading: Tips for the visit
list: Visit the museum first; it explains the layout and makes the ruins easier to read.
Go early in the day; there is little shade on the site.
A guide or the museum staff can point out the drains, warehouse and bead workshops.
Combine Lothal with Nal Sarovar in winter, or with Ahmedabad's old city.

sections.heading: Other Harappan sites in Gujarat
paras: Gujarat has several important Harappan sites. Dholavira in Kutch, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021, is the largest and best presented. Others, such as Rangpur and Surkotada, are less developed for visitors.

items.name: Dholavira
body: The Harappan city in the Rann of Kutch.

sections.heading: When to go
list: November to February: cool, dry and pleasant.
March to June: very hot; visit early in the morning.
July to September: rain can make the site muddy.

sections.heading: The National Maritime Heritage Complex
paras: The Government of India has approved a large National Maritime Heritage Complex near Lothal, with museums on India's maritime history. It is under development; check its current status before planning a visit around it.

safety: Timings, closures and ticket rules are set by the ASI, state archaeology departments or site trusts and change from time to time; check the official website before you go.
The site is open and exposed; carry water and sun protection.
Stay on marked paths and do not walk on excavated walls.

faqs.q: How far is Lothal from Ahmedabad?
faqs.a: About 80 km, around two hours by road.
Most archaeologists interpret the basin as a dockyard, supported by recent studies; a minority view sees it as a reservoir.

faqs.q: Is the Lothal museum open on Friday?
faqs.a: No, the ASI museum is closed on Fridays.
It is on India's Tentative List, not yet inscribed.

faqs.q: How much time do I need at Lothal?
faqs.a: About two to three hours for the site and museum.
It was occupied during the Harappan period, in the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE.

faqs.q: What else can I see near Lothal?
faqs.a: Nal Sarovar bird sanctuary in winter, and Ahmedabad's old city.
